title: How Probing for Problems and Bias Affects Perceptions of AI Chatbot Trustworthiness
authors: Jan Tolsdorf, Alan F. Luo, Monica Kodwani, Junho Eum, Mahmood Sharif, Michelle L. Mazurek, Adam J. Aviv
venueFull: ACM Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency
summary: Interactive study (254 participants, 551 conversations) of how lay users probe chatbots for problems and bias. Participants often failed to surface expected issues, and even limited probing frequently increased trust — a systematic gap in user-driven auditing.

title: “Because I Didn't Touch These and Even Don't Know Why I Should Change These”: Why App Developers Do (Not) Update Apple's Privacy Labels
authors: Arwa Alsahdi, Jialiang Yan, Monica Kodwani, Matthias Fassl, Chris Kanich, Adam J. Aviv
summary: A four-year analysis of privacy-label changes across 926,240 iOS apps, complemented by responses from 128 developers and interviews with 19 developers. Fewer than 6% of apps changed their labels. The study shows how uncertainty about third-party data practices, fragmented responsibility, and limited workflow support can encourage minimal or optimistic disclosure.

title: Safety Perceptions of Generative AI Conversational Agents: Uncovering Perceptual Differences in Trust, Risk, and Fairness
authors: Jan Tolsdorf, Alan F. Luo, Monica Kodwani, Junho Eum, Mahmood Sharif, Michelle L. Mazurek, Adam J. Aviv
venueFull: Symposium on Usable Privacy and Security
summary: Survey of 123 U.S. chatbot users with a new trust–risk–fairness instrument. Identified three user segments — Hesitant Skeptics, Cautious Trusters, and Confident Adopters — with usage frequency, not demographics, the strongest predictor of higher trust and lower perceived risk.

title: On a Scale of 1 to 5, How Reliable Are AI User Studies? A Call for Developing Validated, Meaningful Scales and Metrics about User Perceptions of AI Systems
authors: Jan Tolsdorf, Alan F. Luo, Monica Kodwani, Junho Eum, Mahmood Sharif, Michelle L. Mazurek, Adam J. Aviv
venueFull: IEEE Security & Privacy Workshops — Workshop on Technology and Consumer Protection
summary: Review of 130 AI user studies showing that most measure user perceptions with unvalidated Likert items. Calls for a community repository of validated scales and lays out how to build them.

title: Honesty is the Best Policy: On the Accuracy of Apple Privacy Labels Compared to Apps' Privacy Policies
authors: Mir Masood Ali, David G. Balash, Monica Kodwani, Chris Kanich, Adam J. Aviv
summary: Used fine-tuned language models to compare Apple privacy labels against the apps' own privacy policies, surfacing discrepancies between what labels claim and what the policies actually say.

title: Longitudinal Analysis of Privacy Labels in the Apple App Store
authors: David G. Balash, Mir Masood Ali, Monica Kodwani, Xiaoyuan Wu, Chris Kanich, Adam J. Aviv
summary: Weekly snapshots of 1.6 million apps (July 2021 – October 2022) tracking privacy-label adoption over time. Found roughly 70% adoption, with growth coming mostly from newly listed apps and labels rarely updated after creation — raising questions about their reliability.
